title: Dual of a lisse tensor
statement:
Let $X$ be
smooth of pure dimension
$d$, let $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ and let
$\mathcal L$ be lisse
of finite rank on $X$. Then the Verdier dual satisfies

$$
D_X\bigl(K\otimes^L\mathcal L\bigr)\;\cong\;
D_XK\otimes^L\mathcal L^\vee,
$$

the linear dual $\mathcal L^\vee$ of $\mathcal L$.

proof.text: Use the standing geometric finite-field setting of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$; the schemes in the constructible six-functor setting are separated and of finite type over $k$. Thus $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and finite dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], choose a common finite field $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for $K$ and $\mathcal L$. Write $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi=\varpi_E$ and $B=\varprojlim_n(R/\varpi^n)_X$. The rational category is the raw localization of the completed integral category: choose an integral representative $K_R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], applied to the noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $X$, the integral category underlying $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of the statement is exactly the derived-complete integral category used by the Verdier theorems cited below, with the same completed ring sheaf and reductions; hence the stage-$E$ rationalizations have the same objects and Hom groups. Every object and arrow below is formed at this one stage $E$, so no scalar-extension comparison between the two conventions is used. All the following ringed-site operations are over $B$, not over a discrete constant $R$-sheaf.

source.place: paragraph 1: coefficient categories for the displayed tensor-Hom calculation

proof.text: The underlying space of the Noetherian scheme $X$ has minimal elements in every nonempty set of closed subsets by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; taking complements, every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes. Hence $X$ has finitely many connected components, each open, by [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open]. On each nonempty component choose a geometric point. The finite-field-stage lisse sheaf $\mathcal L_E$ corresponds to a continuous finite-dimensional $E$-representation by [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2). By [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice] choose an invariant finite free $R$-lattice $V_R$. The finite coefficient equivalences in [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1), including their scalar compatibilities, turn $V_R/\varpi^nV_R$ into finite locally free etale sheaves $L_n$ with the actual quotient transitions and $L_{n+1}\otimes_{R/\varpi^{n+1}}R/\varpi^n\cong L_n$. Their rational lisse sheaf is $\mathcal L_E$ by clause (2). Combine these systems on the finitely many disjoint open components; the ranks are bounded and may vary or be zero. This does not assert that a single finite etale cover trivializes the rational sheaf.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second and third bullets, p. 3; repair of blueprint paragraph 2

proof.text: By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], $N=\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*L_n$ is pro-etale locally finite free over $B$, with reductions $N/\varpi^nN=\nu_X^*L_n$, and its rationalization realizes $\mathcal L_E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization](ii) to the single stratum $X$ and the local one-term models $R^r[0]$: $N[0]$ belongs to the exact integral constructible category, including its uniform reduction bounds and compatible etale-origin witnesses. In particular $N$ is perfect as a $B$-complex. Its ordinary dual $N^*=\mathcal Hom_B(N,B)$ is locally $B^r[0]$ with the dual basis and belongs to the same integral category by the same criterion. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], its derived coefficient dual is represented by this ordinary dual: locally the complex of homomorphisms from $B^r[0]$ to any acyclic complex is a finite direct sum of that acyclic complex. These local identifications are the evaluation comparisons, so agree on overlaps.

Let $W_R=\omega_{X,R}$. By [thm-coef-integral-verdier], $C_R=R\mathcal Hom_B(K_R,W_R)=D_{X,R}K_R$ is integral bounded constructible. The lisse tensor $K\otimes^L\mathcal L$ is in $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ by [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus]. To relate the integral calculation to that tensor, use [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] for $(K_R,N)$ and for $(N^*,C_R)$: their ordinary ambient derived tensors over $B$ are already complete and the canonical maps to the completed coefficient tensors are isomorphisms. Its hypotheses hold since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and all four inputs just named are integral constructible.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5; blueprint paragraph 1, definition of Verdier dual

proof.text:
In the ordinary ambient derived category $D(B)$, apply the tensor symmetry of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and then [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] with its variables $(N,K_R,W_R)$. This gives the natural isomorphisms
$$R\mathcal Hom_B(K_R\otimes_B^L N,W_R)\cong R\mathcal Hom_B(N\otimes_B^L K_R,W_R)\cong R\mathcal Hom_B(N,R\mathcal Hom_B(K_R,W_R))=R\mathcal Hom_B(N,C_R).$$
Currying with $N$ as the outer Hom variable avoids any need to assert that tensoring the second variable of an arbitrary internal Hom commutes with a lisse tensor. Neither $K_R$ nor $C_R$ is assumed site-perfect.

Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] to the perfect complex $P=N$ and the arbitrary second argument $C_R$. Inverting its evaluation isomorphism identifies $R\mathcal Hom_B(N,C_R)$ with $N^*\otimes_B^LC_R$. Compose with the preceding currying isomorphism and then the symmetry of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] to obtain
$$D_{X,R}(K_R\otimes_B^LN)\cong C_R\otimes_B^LN^*.$$
The maps here are the global evaluation and currying maps of the cited statements. The local finite-free calculation is used only to check the perfectness hypothesis, not to glue independently chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex; blueprint paragraphs 2-3, evaluation identification

proof.text:
Replace both ordinary tensors in the preceding isomorphism by their completed tensors using Step 4. Apply rationalization, and then the inclusion into the common-stage category. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] these functors carry the completed integral tensor and coefficient internal dual to the tensor and coefficient internal dual at the field stages. By [thm-coef-rational-verdier] and [thm-coef-qbar-verdier], integral Verdier duality similarly becomes precisely $D_X$, and the scalar comparisons identify its dualizing object with $Ra_X^!\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Finally [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus] identifies the image of $N^*=R\mathcal Hom_B(N,B)$ with the degree-zero linear dual $\mathcal L^\vee$, rather than a Tate-twisted Verdier dual. Thus the transported composite is
$$D_X(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)\cong D_XK\otimes^L\mathcal L^\vee.$$
This proves the assertion for the given $K$ and $\mathcal L$. No perfectness of $K$, finite monodromy, or common finite etale trivialization is required.
